newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen sees steady hand Buba policy in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen sees steady hand Buba policy in 1997.

text.p: The Bundesbank will continue to pursue its "steady hand" policy in 1997, council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Thursday, using the phrase the central bank has used to describe its policy over the last year or two.
Jochimsen said in a speech for delivery to a New Year reception in Dusseldorf, "There will be no change in our moderate, steady hand monetary policy in 1997 either."
Jochimsen, who heads the regional central bank based in Dusseldorf, said there were no signs of inflation in the German economy, repeating a widely-held view among Bundesbank council members.
Counting monetary policy's achievements among the assets of the German economy, Jochimsen said the economy was now amply supplied with liquidity to allow a basis for growth.
But he added that the level of investment needed to give the economic upturn a solid base nonetheless remained elusive.

"Unfortunately we must once again take note of the fact that good monetary policy resolutions may be a necessary pre-requisite for investment and so for growth but that it cannot create sufficient conditions in itself," he said.
"To avoid a fatal development on the labour market the marked hesitation over investment in Germany must be overcome," he said.
